title: Explainable ML: SHAP, LIME & Model Debugging
tagline: Explain what your models do and why: glass-box models, feature importance, PDPs, LIME, SHAP and its limits, counterfactuals, saliency maps, and error analysis.
prereqs: Machine Learning. Deep Learning for the Grad-CAM and integrated gradients steps.

steps.title: What explainable AI is
steps.why: Why we need explanations and the main families of methods.

steps.title: Interpretable vs. explainable models
steps.why: Models you can read directly versus explanations added after training.

steps.title: Glass-box models: Explainable Boosting Machines
steps.why: Microsoft Research on additive models that stay readable yet accurate.

steps.title: Permutation feature importance
steps.why: Shuffle one feature, measure the drop in score, coded from scratch.

steps.title: Partial dependence and ICE plots
steps.why: See how predictions change as one feature moves, on average and per row.

steps.title: LIME
steps.why: Fit a simple local model around one prediction to approximate the black box.

steps.title: Shapley values
steps.why: The game theory idea behind SHAP: average each feature's marginal contribution.

steps.title: SHAP in Python
steps.why: Waterfall, force, beeswarm, and dependence plots on a real model.

steps.title: The limits of SHAP
steps.why: Correlated features, baselines, and why SHAP values are not causal effects.

steps.title: Fooling LIME and SHAP
steps.why: Talk showing a biased model can be built to get innocent-looking explanations.

steps.title: Counterfactual explanations
steps.why: The smallest input change that flips a decision, and its link to adversarial examples.

steps.title: Saliency maps with Grad-CAM
steps.why: Highlight the image regions a CNN's prediction depends on.

steps.title: Integrated gradients and feature attribution
steps.why: Stanford lecture on gradient attribution methods and the axioms they satisfy.

steps.title: Debugging models with error analysis
steps.why: Andrew Ng's process for diagnosing bias, variance, and pipeline errors.

projects: Train a gradient-boosted model on a public tabular dataset and compare its SHAP, permutation, and built-in importances in one short report.
Fit an Explainable Boosting Machine and an XGBoost model on the same data, then compare accuracy and what each says about the top three features.
Run Grad-CAM on 20 images a pretrained CNN gets wrong and write down what the heatmaps suggest it was looking at.
